newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court rules against Playboy on cable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court rules against Playboy on cable.

text.p: A federal court on Friday lifted a temporary restraining order on the enforcement of a law that required cable television operators to scramble the video and audio portions of sexually explicit progamming.

On March 4, a federal judge in Delaware had granted Playboy Entertainment Group Inc and Graff-Pay-Per-View Inc a temporary restraining order that prevented the implementation of section 505 of the Communications Decency Act of 1996 until a full trial could be held.

Section 505 requires "a cable television operator to completely scramble or block the video and audio portions of any cable channel...dedicated to sexually explicit programming" or limit its broadcast to the "safe harbor" hours of 10 P.M. to 6 A.M.
Playboy and Graff-Pay-Per-View had argued that the section violated the free speech provision of the First Amendment.

But in a 49-page decision, a three-judge panel of the U.S. District Court of Delaware cited precedent for the compelling "need to protect children from exposure to patently offensive sex-related material."

In lifting the injunction, the judges said that Playboy and Graff Pay-Per-View had failed to prove irreparable harm or "to show that they are likely to succeed in their claim that the provision violates their First Amendment rights to freedom of speech."
The judges include Joseph Farnan of the Delaware District, Jerome Simandle of the New Jersey District, and Jane Roth of the Third Circuit Court of Appeals.
The court did not rule on the issue of constitutionality at this preliminary stage.
